title: Define canonical Transaction taxonomy, scope meaning, and Transfer pair identity

requirements.invariant: Canonical target Transaction classification contains exactly Purchase, Return and Transfer: Purchase means the scope owner paid, Return means the scope owner received money back, and no legacy Sale/paymentToBusiness/Fee/Expense/To Inventory value is representable.

Project scope identifies the Account, Project and authoritative Client owner; Business Inventory identifies the Account/1584 owner. Transfer is project-only and non-cash, and its direct route never includes Business Inventory.

A Transfer route has distinct source and destination Projects in the same Account with the exact same non-null ClientID; the destination is active, Business Inventory and archived/different-Client destinations are invalid, and display-name equality is never evidence.

One logical Transfer identity binds exactly one distinct source Transaction ID and one distinct destination Transaction ID under one operation/correlation identity and one exact route; neither pair identity can be represented as a standalone or same-record Transfer.

Taxonomy, scope, role, economic meaning, route and pair identity are immutable provider-free value objects over typed IDs; impossible cross-field states fail construction and decoding with stable bounded errors rather than raw strings or backend DTOs.

This Phase 1 value boundary is executable with synthetic deterministic evidence while the released Firebase application remains unchanged and no Transaction writer, schema, provider, source transform, hosted resource or production authority is introduced.

items: LedgerTransactionType is the closed purchase/return/transfer set; TransactionEconomicMeaning is derived as scope-owner-paid, scope-owner-received-money-back or non-cash-same-Client-reallocation and is never caller supplied.

TransactionScope is either Business Inventory under one AccountID or Project under exact AccountID/ProjectID/ClientID; TransactionClassification permits standalone Purchase/Return in either scope and source/destination Transfer roles only in Project scope.

ProjectTransferRoute derives exclusively from validated ProjectSummary identity, requires distinct Projects in one Account with exact equal ClientID and an active destination, and retains no display-name authorization evidence.

TransferPairIdentity binds one OperationID, one validated ProjectTransferRoute and distinct source/destination TransactionID values; construction and decoding cannot admit a one-sided, same-record or route-free pair.
TransactionTaxonomyFailure provides stable safe invalid-type/scope/role/route/pair codes without raw IDs, names, paths, source enum text or vendor payloads.

postgresSchema.notApplicable: This Phase 1 provider-free boundary creates no Transaction enum/check, scope columns, pair table, foreign key, uniqueness rule, index, view or migration; the complete Transaction vertical slice must define and verify those separately.

serverHandlers.notApplicable: No RecordPurchase/RecordReturn/TransferItems/correction command, amount, Item line, Invoice effect, lock, transaction, idempotent result or authoritative pair writer is implemented.

dataApiGrants.notApplicable: No relation, view or function is exposed through the Supabase Data API.

rlsPolicies.notApplicable: Same-Account/same-Client value validation is not authorization. No server rows, membership/financial predicate, grants or RLS policies exist in this slice.

syncStreams.notApplicable: No PowerSync Stream, local Transaction table, Transfer-pair download, upload queue or readiness/visibility proof is introduced.

items: Every taxonomy, scope, classification, route and pair value is immutable and Codable; decoding reconstructs through the same cross-field validators.

Canonical sorted-key evidence for representative Project/Inventory Purchase/Return and both Transfer roles plus pair identity round-trips byte-identically without disk, database, network or provider state.

Inventory Transfer, incompatible standalone/Transfer role, cross-Account/cross-Client/same-Project/archived-destination route and duplicate pair-record identity fail atomically without a partial value.

storageMedia.notApplicable: No receipt/Item/Transfer attachment ID, bytes, path, URL, cache, upload, retention or deletion behavior exists.

appMcp.notApplicable: Reusable target values are defined, but no current app enum/filter/card, target query/command DTO, MCP schema/tool, transport or contract-catalog entry is wired.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No legacy Firebase type/scope/movement field is decoded or mapped. Later migration must classify every source row from full evidence, correlate both Transfer halves and quarantine disagreement rather than parse enum text alone.

observabilityRunbooks.notApplicable: Stable local failure codes are contract values only; no telemetry emission, metric, alert or runbook action is added.

items: The implementation remains inside the provider-free LedgerTargetCore and test targets and is not linked by changing either application project.

The slice cannot create a Transaction, write a Transfer pair, choose amount/line/category/Invoice/Space/correction behavior, define schema/provider/migration, activate a feature, deploy, release or cut over.
O-002/O-011–O-015 and O-028–O-032 remain fully open for excluded Transfer effects, provenance, corrections, lifecycle, receipt and posting surfaces.

verification.expected: Exactly three canonical types derive the correct scope-owner/non-cash meanings; standalone Purchase/Return validate in Project and Inventory scope while legacy types and caller-authored meaning remain unrepresentable.

A direct same-Account/same-Client/distinct-Project active-destination route and one Operation-bound distinct source/destination Transaction pair preserve exact typed identity and roles without Business Inventory or name authority.
Representative classifications, route and pair identity round-trip byte-identically through canonical restart and re-run all structural validation without opening local or remote state.

Inventory Transfer, incompatible roles, cross-Account/cross-Client/same-Project/archived-destination routes, duplicate pair record IDs and malformed decoded combinations fail atomically with stable non-enumerating codes.

verification.owner: pull-request CI Isolated target environment job
verification.expected: The exact implementation commit passes conversion traceability, provider/source-contamination and generated-contract checks, the complete target suite, both target builds and clean artifacts without changing an application project or claiming writer, schema, authorization, provider, migration or production behavior.

notes: Decision-independent Phase 1 value foundation only. It implements the confirmed D-001–D-007 classification/scope and structural D-004 pair identity, but no money amount/sign, Item membership, allocation, Invoice/live-charge, Space, correction, lifecycle, schema/RLS/Sync/provider, app/MCP, migration, hosted resource, production access or cutover behavior. D-017 amount conservation and all O-002/O-011–O-015/O-028–O-032 effects remain outside this slice.
